--- Note 45966302 | 2018-06-26 | progress notes ---
GYN Visit  CC: Discuss contraception    Ricky Sidana is a 48 Y female G1P1 here for consultation regarding IUD.  She has a mirena in place. It was placed 5 years ago. She still has ammenorhea from the device.  She wonders if she needs a new one or if she is in menopause  Has had no hotflashes/night sweats.     Jansen history  1 term c-section    GYN history  No history or STDs  Last PAP unsure    Medications - mirena    PMH/PSH/SH reviewed     Visit Vitals  BP 122/78 (Patient site: Right arm, Patient Position: Sitting)   Pulse 106   Ht 4' 11" (1.499 m)   Wt 178 lb 14.4 oz (81.1 kg)   LMP  (LMP Unknown)   BMI 36.13 kg/m²       We discussed diagnosis of menopause and average age of of menopause  We discussed extended use of mirena for 7 years.     After discussion patient elected to replace IUD at this time      IUD REMOVAL and INSERTION PROCEDURE  - pregnancy test today : negative      A complete discussion of the risks and benefits of IUD use and the details of the insertion procedure was held with the patient. We reviewed the risk of infection within 3 weeks of insertion, cramping and irregular bleeding patterns for first 3-6 months, amenorrhea, risk of uterine perforation at time of insertion and expulsion. All questions were answered.  A consent form was signed.      The patient was placed in low lithotomy.  A bimanual examination was done. A speculum was placed.  The IUD strings were grasped with a ring forceps.  And the IUD was removed and noted to be intact.     Next the cervix was swabbed with Betadine.  A single tooth tenaculum was placed on the anterior cervical lip.   The MIRENA IUD was placed to the uterine fundus without difficulty.  The strings were cut to 2 cms.  The tenaculum was removed and hemostasis was ensured.  The speculum was removed.  The patient tolerated the procedure well.    PLAN:   The patient was asked to contact the clinic for any fever/chills/severe pelvic or abdominal pain or  heavy bleeding. She was instructed in how to palpate her IUD strings.    FOLLOW-UP:  She was asked to follow up in ~6 weeks      (V) Face-to-face time with the patient: 30 minutes. (C) Counseling/Coordination of care: 20 minutes regarding Contracpetion options, IUDs and IUD insertion .    Yasmin Didier MD  06/26/2018        


This patient's primary concern falls under: gynecology.
